tagline: Numbers you can defend in the board meeting, with the working shown
intro: An analyst desk for B2B software companies in Southeast Asia. We size markets, pull competitors apart and interview buyers, then hand over a model you can rerun and a memo that says what the numbers mean.
audience: Founders, finance and strategy leads at B2B software companies selling across Singapore, Indonesia, Vietnam and the Philippines, plus the funds that back them.
pricing_note: Fixed-fee studies scoped in a one-page brief, or a monthly desk retainer for teams that need answers every week. Half up front, half on delivery.

services.title: Market sizing models
services.description: A spreadsheet model built bottom-up from buyer counts and spend, cross-checked top-down, with every input sourced and every assumption in one tab you can change.

services.title: Competitor teardowns
services.description: Pricing, packaging, sales motion, hiring and funding for your closest rivals, refreshed each quarter if you want it kept current.

services.title: Buyer interviews
services.description: Structured calls with economic buyers and users in your target accounts, coded and counted, so the qualitative answer comes with a number attached.

services.title: Desk retainer
services.description: A named analyst on call for the questions that come up between board meetings: a new rival, a pricing change, a market you had not considered.

process.title: Scope the question
process.description: A thirty-minute call and a one-page brief: the decision, the market, the deadline and what a good answer looks like.

process.title: Run the queries
process.description: Desk research, data pulls, competitor sign-ups and buyer calls, logged in a source sheet as we go, with a check-in halfway.

process.title: Hand over the model
process.description: A memo that leads with the answer, the model behind it and an hour with your team to stress-test the assumptions together.

proof.text: Our investors stopped questioning the market size once they could change the inputs themselves.
proof.source: Chief financial officer, a Singapore payroll platform (sample)

proof.text: The quarterly teardown is the most read document in our sales channel.
proof.source: Revenue lead, a Jakarta logistics start-up (sample)

proof.text: Fast, careful and honest about what the data could not tell us.
